title: Bound Retry Amplification
description: Three nested service layers each make up to three attempts, including the first attempt, whenever their downstream call fails. In the worst case, how many calls can one top-level request cause to the deepest service?

options.text: 3, because each layer has the same limit.
options.explanation: A local attempt limit does not cover attempts made independently by downstream layers.
Each attempt at one layer can trigger all attempts at the next, so the counts multiply rather than add.

options.text: 27; use a shared deadline and a chosen retry layer to bound amplification.
options.explanation: Three attempts at each of three layers can produce 3 x 3 x 3 = 27 deepest calls. Jitter spreads their timing but does not reduce this worst-case count by itself.
Backoff changes when attempts occur, not how many are permitted.
